title: Bhai Mani Singh at Amritsar and the Prophecy of Dismemberment

blocks.text: Bhai Mani Singh appears here as a learned, disciplined, and deeply trusted servant of the Panth. His authority is rooted in devotion, scriptural knowledge, and closeness to the Guru’s mission, making him a figure of moral as well as institutional weight.

The page then turns to his formal responsibilities under Mata Sundari’s direction. He is sent to Amritsar to guide the sangat, supervise sacred administration, and take control of the offerings at Amritsar so that gifts placed before the Guru may be directed toward the needs of the community.

The closing movement becomes darker and more prophetic. Because Mani Singh is said to have altered the recension on his own initiative, the sangat pronounces that his body will one day be cut limb by limb, foreshadowing the martyrdom that now begins to draw near.
